_doc: AUTHORITATIVE contract for the relationship between installable skill-template
The two surfaces are NOT a subtree mirror. install.py stamps template paths to
DIFFERENT live paths, so a raw relative-path or `diff -rq` comparison is not an
authoritative parity model — it reports correctly-mapped trees as absent. Every
mapping below is transcribed from the stamp() calls in install.py's main(),
which are the source of truth; docs describe that mapping but do not define it.
Every governed path resolves to exactly one typed relation. An added, removed,
or divergent governed path with no declared relation is NON-PASS or CNO — never

authority.note: If install.py's stamp calls change, this contract is stale and the verifier must be updated with it.

relations.EXACT_MIRROR: Mapped content identity is required. Fails closed on divergent bytes and on a counterpart missing from either surface.
relations.CONTRACT_ONLY: Bodies may diverge, but a NAMED verifier proves a NAMED property. The property, not the filename, is the obligation.
relations.TEMPLATE_SCAFFOLD: The template copy is a deliberate generic placeholder that a stamped repo is expected to replace. Body divergence is correct; any shared API contract is declared separately and still enforced.
relations.USER_OWNED: Stamped once as a starter, then owned by the target repo. install.py skips it when it already exists, so divergence is the designed steady state.
relations.LIVE_ONLY: Present on the live surface by design and never stamped. Must be declared to stay distinguishable from an omitted stamping substrate.

surfaces.rationale: install.md:22 — the template module tree carries 'all low-level logic', and the twelve starter ADWs are stamped verbatim. This is the substrate a stamped repo runs on, so one-sided edits are drift by default.
surfaces.exclude_reason: These live subtrees are stamped from DIFFERENT template roots, or are live-only. Each excluded prefix must be claimed by another surface or by live_only below; an unclaimed exclusion is a silent escape and is refused.

surfaces.rationale: Non-isomorphic mapping: template root and live root differ. A stamped repo must receive the same agent instructions the live surface runs, including any mechanism notice that describes runtime behaviour such as out-of-scope write rollback.
Non-isomorphic mapping. Pi extensions backing declared tools must be identical, or a stamped roster declares a tool its extension cannot serve.
The agent roster. install.md:19 marks it user-owned and install.md:34 warns that --force overwrites operator edits, so template and live are meant to diverge the moment it is stamped.

Non-isomorphic mapping: templates/env.sample stamps to a DOTFILE at the repo root. The template documents provider keys generically ('WHICH KEYS YOU NEED DEPENDS ON YOUR ROSTER'); the live copy is specific to this repo's single-provider OpenRouter setup. install.py skips it when present.
surfaces.evidence: .claude/skills/sssf/scripts/install.py stamp() skip-if-exists; template env.sample header vs live .env.sample header

surfaces.rationale: Starter recipes only. install.py's own comment says it is 'Skipped like any other file if the repo already has a justfile', and the live copy carries repo-specific shell settings and application recipes.

overrides.rationale: The template copy ships placeholder blocks that exit 0 and announce they are fake, because a stamped repo cannot guess its own test runner and a wrong-but-plausible command that silently passes is worse than one that says so. The live copy is wired to this repo's real commands. Copying either body over the other is a defect, not a repair.

contract.property: Both surfaces must define the shared quality API as module-level callables, so every stamped ADW call site resolves on both surfaces even though the bodies differ.
contract.corroborating_property: resolves imported adw_modules attributes per surface, so a call site naming a removed export fails there too
contract.note: The named property is the obligation. A filename or a validator's name is not proof, which is why the exact exports and the exact verifier symbol are written down here.

coupled.rationale: pi_json_adapter imports subprocess_supervisor directly, so a stamped state carrying the adapter without its supervisor is broken on import. They stamp together or not at all.

live_only.rationale: Alternate roster. install.py stamps exactly one config; additional rosters are selected with --config or SSSF_CONFIG and are a live-surface concept.
live_only.evidence: .claude/skills/sssf/references/config.md:5; docs/baseline/PROOF_MATRIX.md:99 counts five rosters as a live-surface property

live_only.rationale: Created at runtime and gitignored by install.py's ensure_gitignore; never stamped.
